identity.trade: Sheep and spinning: Thistledown's wethers graze the downs, and its spinners sell the finest thread on the outer road.

greeting: Reeve here. Yes, it is as dull as it sounds. Ask anyway.
If a sheep looks at you, look back. They are judging.
rumour: Strangers stop here more than they used to. Not all of them buy anything.
The shepherds talk of a white ewe that leads the flock where nobody sends it.
A lamb was born with silver wool. It lasted a day.

opinions.enid_brook: Enid is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.morning: Morning. The flock is out and the dogs are bored.

dialogue.aside: Argh! Oh, it is you. Sorry. The kettle and I had words. Sit.

greeting: Sit anywhere that is not wet. The wet ones are the regulars.
Strangers in Thistledown get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Shepherds come in smelling of lanolin and leave smelling of ale. Fair trade.
Somebody paid in old coin last night. Very old. Nobody knew the king on it.
A stray lamb turned up at the fold, not ours, with a ribbon on its neck. The ribbon was silk.
Every few years Thistledown has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.dane_clay: Dane undercuts me. I forgive Dane. Mostly.

time.evening: Folding time. The sheep go in and the stories come out.

dialogue.aside: Mind the order of things, friend. There. Now we can talk.

greeting: Bring iron or bring coin. Preferably iron.
Welcome to Thistledown. Mind the Thistledown Fold. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Shears, bells and crooks. Every blade in the fold passed my anvil.
Plough blades sell slow and spear heads sell fast. I do not like what that says.
Fleece grades are down. The buyers blame the shepherds. The shepherds blame the grass.

opinions.flora_lambert: Flora has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Flora.
opinions.hilde_yardley: Hilde undercuts me. I forgive Hilde. Mostly.

time.night: Quiet night. Listen for the bell. If it stops, shout.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. I would say nice day, but it is not, and you would know.

greeting: Everything has a price. Some of it is even written down.
Watch where you step. The flock has right of way.
rumour: Shears, salt and string. A shepherd can make anything from those.
Folk buy more than they need, then bring half back. Fear shops strangely.
Wool prices rose last week and fell again before the carters left. Somebody is gaming the buyers.
A stranger asked at the Thistledown Fold for the oldest person in Thistledown. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.dane_clay: Dane undercuts me. I forgive Dane. Mostly.
opinions.radley_kettle: Radley keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.rain: Rain. Wool soaks and stays wet. We smell of sheep and regret.

dialogue.aside: Hmph. You again. Fine. Sit. I did not say I was glad.

greeting: You are somebody's grandchild. I can tell by the walk.
Thistledown is sheep and spinners. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: When I was young the stones sang at dusk. Now they hum, like someone ill.
The old drove road is quieter than it should be. No bells, no dust, no drovers.
The spinners sing while they work. The songs are older than the village.

opinions.flora_lambert: Flora keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.morning: Morning. The flock is out and the dogs are bored.

dialogue.aside: Friend! I have a plan. It is a terrible plan. It is going to be wonderful.

greeting: Fleece by the stone, gossip free.
The downs are windy, the wool is warm and the dogs know best.
rumour: Prices are down. The wolves are bolder past the downs.
The dogs refuse the east pasture. They sit at the gate and whine.

opinions.derwin_rimmer: Derwin lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.odell_fellows: Odell knows the trade. I will say that for Odell.

time.evening: Folding time. The sheep go in and the stories come out.

dialogue.aside: A friend is a rare coin. I have spent worse.

greeting: Mind the wool. It sticks to everything, opinions especially.
First time in Thistledown? The Thistledown Fold is the place to start.
rumour: A cart of fleece arrived damp. Someone left it in the rain on purpose, I think.
A line of cairns appeared on the ridge. We did not build them.
Sheep vanish near the downs' old barrow and nobody goes looking.

opinions.barda_rimmer: Barda is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.
opinions.dalla_wythe: Dalla keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.night: Quiet night. Listen for the bell. If it stops, shout.

dialogue.aside: Good to see you. Now, what do you need, and what can you spare?

greeting: Wool does not shear itself. More is the pity.
The Thistledown Fold is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Count at dusk, count at dawn, count when the dog looks worried.
The wolves took no sheep this month. They took the bell ram. Only the bell ram.
Whatever you hear about Thistledown, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.derwin_rimmer: Derwin works hard and talks harder.
opinions.osric_brook: Osric knows the trade. I will say that for Osric.

time.rain: Rain. Wool soaks and stays wet. We smell of sheep and regret.

dialogue.aside: I do not say this often. It is good to see a face I do not need to avoid.

greeting: Do not stand between a ewe and her lamb. She will not read the sign.
Folk come to Thistledown for sheep and spinners. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: The wethers stand all night facing the same hill. I have not asked why.
A ewe lambed twins and went silent. Ewes are never silent.

opinions.dalla_wythe: Dalla knows the trade. I will say that for Dalla.
opinions.derwin_rimmer: Derwin works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Morning. The flock is out and the dogs are bored.

dialogue.aside: Up before dawn, friend? Then you saw the best of the day. I saw it first.

greeting: Quiet, lad. Not you. The dog.
Thistledown is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Counted forty, home came thirty-nine. The dog looks guilty.
Shearing went well, but the wool came off with a grey tint. Not age. Something in the grass.
Folk say Thistledown was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.marden_lyle: Marden works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Folding time. The sheep go in and the stories come out.

dialogue.aside: Tell me everything. No, truly. I will not ask twice. I will ask three times.

greeting: Mind the pail, it is still warm.
You will hear Thistledown before you see it. Ask at the Thistledown Fold.
rumour: Milk soured overnight in two houses. The cellar is cold. It is not the cellar.
The Thistledown Fold has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

opinions.morwen_thackeray: Morwen works hard and talks harder.
opinions.osric_brook: Osric knows the trade. I will say that for Osric.

time.night: Quiet night. Listen for the bell. If it stops, shout.

dialogue.aside: Punctual as ever, friend. I admire that. I also resent it.

greeting: The cream is the cream. You can pay for it or admire it.
rumour: Butter came out grey twice this week. The churn is clean. The cows are tired.
Thistledown lives by sheep and spinners. When that fails, so do we.

opinions.enid_brook: Enid and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.
opinions.hugh_greaves: Hugh works hard and talks harder.

time.rain: Rain. Wool soaks and stays wet. We smell of sheep and regret.

greeting: Do not touch the rind. The rind is working.
rumour: Merchants pay well and ask no questions about the age. They get what they pay for.
The Thistledown Fold drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.

opinions.dalla_wythe: Dalla knows the trade. I will say that for Dalla.
opinions.derwin_rimmer: Derwin works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Morning. The flock is out and the dogs are bored.

dialogue.aside: Close the door, friend. Gently. There. Now we can speak.

greeting: Do you have a dog? I do not have a dog. Yet.
rumour: Our dog knows something and will not say what.
Shearing went well, but the wool came off with a grey tint. Not age. Something in the grass.

opinions.osric_brook: Osric is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.
opinions.oswin_fleece: I would trust Oswin with a purse. A small one.

greeting: I am not lost. I am exploring.
rumour: The big kids say there is a ghost in the barn. I have not checked. Yet.
Fleece grades are down. The buyers blame the shepherds. The shepherds blame the grass.

opinions.derwin_rimmer: Derwin and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

clues.note: A fleece sack half emptied behind the fold, the mouth re-tied in a hurry.
Hoof prints mixed with boot prints. The animals were walked, not driven.
The gate rope is cut, not frayed. The edge is clean.

stashes.say: You lift three wheels from the cool shelf.
